_source: The 14 allergens are set by retained Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011, Annex II, and the Food Information Regulations 2014. PPDS rules (Natasha's Law) apply from 1 October 2021. See the Food Standards Agency's allergen guidance for food businesses.
_recheckDays_note: 90 days is this app's re-check habit, not a legal limit. Check labels again whenever a supplier, brand or product changes.

allergens.name: Celery
allergens.plain: Celery stalks, leaves, seeds and root (celeriac). Often in stock, soups, salads and celery salt.

allergens.name: Cereals containing gluten
allergens.plain: Wheat (including spelt and Khorasan wheat), rye, barley and oats. Often in bread, pasta, batter, sauces and soups.

allergens.name: Crustaceans
allergens.plain: Prawns, crab, lobster, crayfish and similar. Often in shrimp paste and some Thai and Chinese dishes.

allergens.name: Eggs
allergens.plain: Eggs from any bird. Often in cakes, mayonnaise, pasta, mousse, glazes and some sauces.

allergens.name: Fish
allergens.plain: Any fish. Often in Worcestershire sauce, fish sauce, pizzas, relishes and salad dressings.

allergens.name: Lupin
allergens.plain: Lupin flour and seeds. Sometimes in bread, pastry and pasta.

allergens.name: Milk
allergens.plain: Cow's milk and milk from other animals, and anything made from it: butter, cheese, cream, yoghurt, whey.

allergens.name: Molluscs
allergens.plain: Mussels, oysters, squid, snails and similar. Often in oyster sauce and fish stews.

allergens.name: Mustard
allergens.plain: Mustard seeds, powder and liquid mustard. Often in dressings, marinades, sauces and curries.

allergens.name: Tree nuts
allergens.plain: Almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts, cashews, pecans, Brazil nuts, pistachios and macadamia (Queensland) nuts. Often in pesto, marzipan, praline and nut oils.
allergens._note: A plain 'nuts' on a label is treated as tree nuts. Pine nuts and coconut are not one of the 14.

allergens.name: Peanuts
allergens.plain: Peanuts (groundnuts) and peanut oil. Often in satay, sauces, cakes and some Asian dishes.

allergens.name: Sesame
allergens.plain: Sesame seeds and sesame oil. Often in bread, breadsticks, hummus (tahini) and stir-fries.

allergens.name: Soya
allergens.plain: Soya beans and anything made from them: tofu, soy sauce, edamame, miso. Often in desserts, ice cream and vegetarian products.

allergens.name: Sulphur dioxide and sulphites (over 10 mg/kg or 10 mg/litre)
allergens.plain: A preservative at more than 10 mg per kg or litre. Often in dried fruit, wine, beer, vinegar, sausages and soft drinks.
allergens._note: Only declared above 10 mg/kg or 10 mg/litre. If a label names sulphites, treat the product as containing them.

_labelFormats_note: Sizes match common A4 label sheets. Print one test sheet on plain paper with outlines on, hold it over your labels, and check the margins for your printer.

ppds._minFontPt_note: The law asks for an x-height of at least 1.2 mm (0.9 mm if the pack's largest surface is under 80 cm²). 1.2 mm is about 6.5 pt in the system font. Needs checking against your own printed labels.
requirements: The full ingredients list, biggest by weight first.
The 14 allergens emphasised every time they appear (this app uses CAPITALS in bold).

matrix.title: Allergen matrix
matrix.legend: ✓ = contains this allergen.   may = may contain it (cross-contact risk).   Blank = not in our recipe.
matrix.staffNote: Ask a member of staff before you order if you have a food allergy or intolerance.
matrix.disclaimer: Made from our ingredient labels. Recipes and suppliers can change. Check this matrix every time a recipe or supplier changes.
